cohort: The study included 200 pregnant women, aged 20-35 years, with group A having a history of first trimester bleeding and group B having no such history, excluding those with twin pregnancy, congenital uterine anomaly, large leiomyomata, chronic or gestational diabetes, hypertension, vaginal spotting with an open cervix, polyhydramnios, or previous history of preterm labor/PPROM.
finding: First trimester threatened miscarriage was significantly associated with both preterm delivery (58% in exposed group vs 17% in unexposed group) and PPROM (19% in exposed group vs 8% in unexposed group).
